_doc: ROIs for the Quake start-map archway torch-presence gate. See docs/misc/2026-09-03-quake-torch-regression-archaeology.md section 5.1.
_scale_rule: multiply all boxes by (frame_width / 1920); HDMI tick grabs are 3840x2160 -> factor 2
_box_format: [x0, y0, x1, y1] inclusive-exclusive, in the 1920x1080 basis
_pass_rule: for each require:true ROI, count pixels with R>100 && R>G+20 && R>B+20 (warm-biased pixel brighter than the surrounding stone); ROI passes at >=8 such pixels; the frame passes when both required ROIs pass; the CYCLE passes when >=2 frames pass (the flame animates and a single grab can tear)
_pass_rule_calibration: CORRECTED 2026-09-03 after implementing scripts/check-torch-rois.py. The original rule (R>180 && R>G+40 && G>B+20, an orange flame core) counts ZERO pixels in the host reference ITSELF: at the start map light level the flame sprite renders pale warm grey peaking near R=123, not saturated orange. It would have failed a known-good frame. Measured with the corrected rule: reference 17 and 11 lit px; vkQuake grab (torches absent) 0 and 0, peaking R=63..74 -- about 2x separation in peak brightness.
_viewpoint_rule: These are FIXED boxes, so they only mean anything for a frame taken at the reference viewpoint. The checker first compares a 160x90 grey thumbnail against the reference and reports UNUSABLE above mae 8.0. Measured: reference vs itself 0.0; vkQuake grabs sitting at spawn ~3.5; quakespasm frames from Quake DEMO ATTRACT MODE (what the engine shows when left at the menu) 14-17. So idle HDMI ticks are NOT gradeable -- capture with an explicit `+map start`.

rois._why: DO NOT COUNT THIS. It is a MOVING projectile on a periodic timer, so it is present in some frames and absent in others, and it looks like an orange/red flame. On 2026-08-22 this decoy was mistaken for a restored wall torch and closed the bug on a false positive (grab 20260822-200435-vkq-torchfix-tick.png). It is listed here only so a future checker excludes it explicitly.
